notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). Model-authored and unreviewed. The card's family-config GymnasiumDriver fits: the upstream entry src.ot2.ot2_gym_wrapper:OT2Env is a Gymnasium environment over the repository's PyBullet OT-2 digital twin (src/ot2/sim_class.py:12). gymnasium and pybullet are not installed where the gate runs and requirements.txt:1-17 lists both, so the fake backend is the package's own pure Python kinematic OT2Env stand-in (fake.py) and the upstream environment was not run or compared with it; no sim backend is offered. The fake declares F0 (kinematic, no simulated clock); its fidelity gaps list what is not modelled, that observations are lists instead of float32 numpy arrays, and that the upstream reset accepts only seed (src/ot2/ot2_gym_wrapper.py:38), so cap.world.reset.v1 options are not supported and the bridge falls back to a seedless reset. The observation is the full six values of the upstream Box(shape=(6,)) and the action is the full three-vector, so no array is reduced. No hardware backend and no site-limits overlay: the device is simulated R0 and the only bound is the bridge-derived action space. Five warnings are expected of a Gymnasium family driver (PLAYBOOK.md section 8): G6.NO_NATIVE_CALL for cap.world.seed.v1 (the seed sets the next reset) and four G8.NO_UNIT for bridge-derived inputs (ticks, seed twice, and action.values[*] because this action space is Box, not Discrete). Only catalogue classes are used, so there are no catalogue requests. gate.digest is the digest the check printed; check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package.
